title: Toolchain Conductor: API for multi-tool orchestration, injection semantics, and retry ergonomics
author: Ava Lin
description:
Motivation: previous function-calling / tool-calling ergonomics made multi-tool flows brittle in the face of partial failures, streaming tool outputs, and heterogeneous retry requirements. This PR introduces the Toolchain Conductor API and runtime changes to make multi-tool orchestration explicit, safer, and simpler for SDK consumers while improving streaming stability and OpenAI-compat structured-output behavior.

What changed (high level):
- New top-level 'toolchain' field in the API surface that lets callers declare a directed sequence/graph of tool invocations and per-tool execution policies (parallelizable, ordered-inject, idempotency-token, retry-policy).
- Explicit 'inject_policy' semantics for how tool results are merged back into the LLM input: append-only buffer, deterministic slot injection (index by tool name), and optional merge hooks for user-supplied merge functions.
- Streaming improvements: tools now emit chunked 'partial_result' events with stable markers; the runtime buffers/flushes partials per client backpressure window to avoid garbled interleaving in streamed chat responses.
- Retry ergonomics: per-tool idempotency tokens and 'retry-hints' (max_attempts, backoff_strategy, retry_on_partial) allow safe retries without double-injecting results or re-running non-idempotent side effects. The conductor coordinates token usage and mirrors idempotency onto downstream tool invocations.
- Parallel execution: 'concurrency_hint' allows the runtime to safely execute independent tools in parallel with an ordering-affinity map to preserve deterministic injection when required. The conductor produces a canonical merge order for cases where results are required in the prompt.
- OpenAI compatibility: function-calling framing updated to support nested structured outputs produced by ensembles of tools; the compat layer maps conductor outputs into the old function-calling response shape and emits a new 'toolchain_metadata' field describing per-tool statuses for consumers that opt-in.
- Observability: added per-tool metrics (latency_p50/p95, injection_failures, retry_count), conductor-level tracing spans, and new dashboard panels.
- Tests & docs: integration tests for partial-stream recovery, idempotent retry flows, and examples in SDKs plus updated API reference.

Why this is safer: callers can opt into strict injection ordering, idempotency enforcement, and per-tool retry controls which prevents subtle duplication bugs (e.g., re-invoking a billing API or re-applying a mutation). The explicit conductor model also makes reasoning about streaming boundaries and backpressure easier for client implementers.

Backward compat: default runtime behavior preserves prior semantics for simple single-tool calls; the new toolchain surface is opt-in. OpenAI-compat responses remain available but with additional metadata when the conductor is used.

Next steps: small follow-ups to expose a higher-level SDK builder (ToolchainBuilder) and an admin flag to enable strict deterministic injection across replicas (ENG-7510).

review_thread: Diego Martinez (review): Overall looks good — can you clarify failure semantics when a tool returns a partial result and then errors?

Ava Lin (author): we introduced 'partial_result' + terminal 'error' event; the conductor will surface the partial and then emit a failure status for that tool. Retry policy 'retry_on_partial' controls if we re-run from the last safe boundary.
Samiya Khan (request_changes): we need stronger guarantees that retries won't double-inject. Can you show where we dedupe injects?
Ava Lin: added idempotency token propagation and an inject ledger in injector.go with tests demonstrating dedupe across retries. See new unit test 'test_injector_dedupe'.
Tom Becker (comment): please ensure this doesn't regress streaming throughput; consider a non-blocking flush path for large partial streams.
Ava Lin: added non-blocking flush that stream-queues large partials and defers injection ordering decisions to the conductor's merge step; added perf test simulating 100 concurrent partial streams.
merge_commit: aa7c3b4: squash: Toolchain Conductor and retry ergonomics
release_notes: Added a new opt-in Toolchain Conductor API for multi-tool orchestration: per-tool retry policies, idempotency tokens, deterministic injection options, streaming partial_result semantics, and improved OpenAI-compat structured output mapping. Default single-tool behavior unchanged.
notes_for_release: This is opt-in. SDKs (Python/TS) expose ToolchainBuilder examples in docs/api/toolchain.md. Admins who want strict deterministic injection across replicas should follow ENG-7510 for enabling the cluster-wide flag.
qa_notes: Manual QA performed for: partial stream recovery, retry-on-partial flows, parallel execution deadlocks. Added integration tests that run in CI.
